title: Wheeze and high pressures after a new drug
summary: A 58-year-old ventilated man develops wheeze, high peak pressures and a slow expiratory flow.
rationale: Airway narrowing raises resistance, mostly in expiration, so Ppk rises, Pplat stays normal and gas trapping builds slowly. A bronchodilator reduces resistance within minutes; increasing the rate makes trapping worse. Headless engine check on the starting settings and after the named actions: untouched by 2 min: PaCO2 48, pH 7.32, SpO2 93%, Pplat 21, auto-PEEP 2.7, SBP 89; untouched by 30 min: PaCO2 51, pH 7.30, SpO2 93%, Pplat 21, auto-PEEP 2.7, SBP 89; reasonable management by 30 min: PaCO2 50, pH 7.31, SpO2 94%, Pplat 18, SBP 99; typical mistake by 30 min: PaCO2 35, pH 7.43, SpO2 93%, Pplat 25, auto-PEEP 6.7, SBP 79. Values for an arm whose case ended early (improved or deteriorated trigger) are the values when it ended.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: Bronchospasm raises peak pressure with a normal plateau; give bronchodilator and watch for air trapping rather than raising the rate

source: The Ventilator Book 3e (alarms / troubleshooting and respiratory mechanics chapters, numbers unverified); Marino ICU Book 2025 (ventilator-associated complications and airway pressure chapters, unverified); Nunn & Lumb 9e (resistance and compliance chapters, unverified); Hess DR. Respir Care 2014;59:1773-94 (peak minus plateau pressure); Marino ICU Book 2025 (acute severe asthma / bronchospasm, number unverified). Expiratory resistance 45 and inspiratory 22 are teaching assumptions (unverified).

changes.vignette: Male 58, 172 cm, 75 kg. VC 420 mL, RR 18, PEEP 8, FiO2 0.4. Wheeze began after a new antibiotic infusion.

patient.presentingStory: Ventilated for pneumonia. About 10 minutes after starting a new antibiotic the nurse hears wheeze, and the high-pressure alarm is sounding. Blood pressure is slightly lower.
patient.history: Pneumonia, penicillin allergy label not confirmed. Full escalation.

findings.examine: Sedated. Widespread expiratory wheeze both sides, prolonged expiration, no rash. Equal chest movement. Tube at 22 cm at the teeth.
findings.cxr: Tube 4 cm above the carina, right lower zone consolidation, hyperinflated lungs, no pneumothorax.

evidence.claim: Bronchospasm raises airway resistance; peak pressure rises while plateau pressure does not.
evidence.source: Marino PL. Marino's The ICU Book, 2025 edition (chapter on ventilator troubleshooting; number unverified)

evidence.claim: Measurement of plateau pressure via inspiratory hold differentiates high resistance (elevated Ppeak, normal Pplat) from low compliance (both Ppeak and Pplat elevated).
evidence.source: Hess DR. Respiratory mechanics in the mechanically ventilated patient. Respir Care 2014;59(11):1773-1794

actions.text: Salbutamol given through the circuit. The wheeze is easing.
The suction catheter passes freely to the carina and returns scant clear secretions. The pressures are unchanged.
The senior says: what do the peak and plateau pressures show, and where does the tube sit? Work through the DOPE checklist.
Furosemide 40 mg given and the urine output rises a little. There is no immediate change in the airway pressures.

then.reason: The cause of the high airway pressure was found and treated; pressures, blood pressure and oxygenation have recovered.
The high airway pressure was not corrected, and the patient became profoundly hypotensive or hypoxaemic.

then.detail: A high peak airway pressure persisted for 7 minutes without a structured check (DOPE: tube, obstruction, pneumothorax, equipment) and an inspiratory hold to separate resistance from compliance.

rubric.description: Examined the patient within 8 minutes of the alarm
Brought peak pressure to 32 cmH2O or below
Checked a blood gas within 20 minutes

keyPoints: Wheeze with high peak pressure, normal plateau and a long expiratory phase points to bronchospasm; stop the likely trigger and give a bronchodilator.
Raising the rate shortens expiration and causes air trapping and hypotension.
Reassess the pressures and the flow-time waveform after the bronchodilator.
